text: 12. In the early hours of a 1972 morning, a group of men in tracksuits were struggling to hoist heavy duffel bags over a six-foot chain-link fence at the Olympic Village. In one of history’s most surreal moments of irony, they were spotted by a group of "night-owl" American athletes returning from a night of partying. Assuming these were fellow competitors who had also missed their curfew, the Americans joked with the men and actually helped them lift their bags—which were packed with AK-47s—over the barrier.Once inside the dormitory, the nightmare began. X, despite having already sustained a horrific gunshot wound to his face during the initial break-in, was forced to act as a "human key" for the intruders. As they marched him down the corridor at gunpoint to identify his colleagues, he faced a split-second "Sophie’s Choice" at every door.He intentionally bypassed "Apartment 2," knowing it contained the older, more vulnerable officials of his delegation. Instead, he steered the gunmen toward "Apartment 3," which housed the team’s most formidable physical specimens—the wrestlers and weightlifters. He hoped their raw power and combat training would provide a window for a counter-offensive. While his tactical deception allowed one teammate to escape during the ensuing struggle, it ultimately led to X being executed by his captors.Identify X, the courageous coach who sacrificed his life to lead the intruders into a trap

13. In 1956, just weeks after a Soviet invasion of Budapest, the Hungarian and Soviet teams met in a semi-final match of a grueling water sport. The tension was so high that the match had to be stopped when a Hungarian star emerged with a face covered in blood, turning the water pink and nearly inciting a riot in the stands. By what name is this infamous match known?
